title: Latency-aware service-class borrowing admission controller with soft degrade paths
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: We need an admission controller that is aware of end-to-end latency SLOs and can reallocate short-term capacity between service classes (e.g., interactive chat, background embeddings, batch rerank) during spikes. Existing token-bucket admission+priority queues are effective, but when regions experience transient overloads or cross-region failovers we see brittle sudden drops for lower-priority classes and unexpected tail latency regressions for high-priority traffic. This ticket designs and implements a 'service-class borrowing' mechanism paired with soft degrade paths and circuit-breaker integration.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Controller enforces per-class latency SLO targets (p99/p95) under synthetic spike tests, 2) Borrowing rules allow higher-util classes to temporarily take capacity from lower-util classes without starving them completely, 3) Soft degrade modes like token slim-down, compacting structured output, and queueing hints are triggered gracefully, 4) Integration tests cover multi-region failover scenario with traffic shift and canary shows no more than 1.5x increase in p99 for high-priority traffic, 5) Rollout docs, dashboards, and runbook are published.
design_summary:
- Maintain a lightweight per-class reservoir (credit pool) and a global reclaim pool per-region. Credits are filled at steady-state rate tied to allocated throughput. During spikes, higher-priority classes may borrow from lower-priority reservoirs subject to: maximum borrow fraction, time-window decay, and repayment policy.
- Admission decision uses a latency headroom estimator: we sample recent latency percentiles per class and region and compute headroom margin vs SLO. If headroom < threshold, request is admitted only if borrowing tokens are available and an estimated degrade action is acceptable.
- Soft degrade actions are prioritized (1. reduce max output tokens, 2. enable compact embeddings, 3. fall back to cheaper model variant, 4. queue with adaptive retry). Degrade actions are reversed when headroom recovers.
- Circuit breaker integration: breach events (sustained headroom < 0) trip a class-level CB which prevents borrowing to avoid global exhaustion. CB state is replicated through the control plane and acts as input to multi-region failover decisions.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Borrowing increases coupling between tenants/service classes; we mitigate via strict caps and repayment windows.
- Increased complexity in admission decision could add micro-latency; design favors O(1) checks with bounded lookups and metrics for sampling.
- Risk of oscillation when multiple classes borrow simultaneously; we'll use dampening (exponential backoff to borrow frequency) and 'grace windows' to stabilize.
- Multi-region replication lag may cause transient misallocation after failover; we intentionally prefer conservative defaults on cross-region borrow during a failover event.
implementation_plan: 1) RFC + detailed sequence diagrams (link below) -> 2) control-plane schema changes for per-class reservoirs -> 3) admission controller shim in front of runtime worker -> 4) unit + stress tests with 'chaos' scenarios -> 5) canary rollout in us-west-2 region with synthetic spike generator -> 6) global rollout with per-region tuning.
